title: Power Apps: row summaries in model-driven apps reach GCC and GCC High
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap scope, licensing and metered cost assessment, and both configuration paths are supported. It appropriately reports the conflicting default-state documentation; minor corrections should make the planned availability explicit and acknowledge conflicting guidance about table-wide versus per-form configuration.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Row summaries read record data and generate a short natural-language overview.
claims.quote: The feature reads the data on the current record and generates a short, natural-language summary that highlights key information

claims.claim: Summaries appear in the Insights bar on main forms.
claims.quote: From the **Insights** bar at the top of main forms.

claims.claim: Users access summaries from view pages through the Summary action.
claims.quote: From view pages by selecting the inline **Summary** action in the grid, which opens the summary for a record in a modal popup.

claims.claim: Makers configure a table's summary prompt and specify the columns to summarise.
claims.quote: Write a custom prompt to specify which columns should be included in a Copilot‑generated row summary.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Power Platform Copilot FAQ says Copilot adheres to existing data permissions and policies.
claims.quote: Copilot adheres to existing data permissions and policies

claims.claim: That FAQ says Copilot responses use only data the user personally can access.

claims.claim: Learn documents a column-security limitation for form fill assistance.

claims.claim: Generated summaries may be wrong.
claims.quote: AI-generated content can have mistakes

claims.claim: Government-specific pricing for this row-summary rollout has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "government" "pricing"; "row summaries" "GCC" default setting pricing. Opened record-summaries, faq-record-summaries, AI Builder administer-licensing and powerapps-us-government; no government row-summary rate found.

claims.claim: Government terms may differ from the general Power Apps offering.
claims.quote: It defines the unique commitments of this service and the differences from Power Apps offerings that have been available to our customers since October 2016.

claims.claim: The arrival default for the government expansion is not stated unambiguously, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "GCC High" setting default; "row summaries" "GCC" default setting pricing. Read roadmap, record-summaries, faq-record-summaries and powerapps-us-government; general enablement/default statements differ, with no government rollout default.

claims.claim: The row-summary user guide says a Power Platform administrator must enable Row summaries for the environment.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable **Row summaries** for the environment in the Power Platform admin center under **Copilot** > **Settings** > **Power Apps** > **Summary**.

claims.claim: The row-summary FAQ says the AI insight cards environment setting is on by default.
claims.quote: The **AI insight cards** environment setting that enables row summaries is on by default.

claims.claim: The FAQ says makers still need to configure and turn on summary prompts on individual tables.
claims.quote: Makers still need to configure and turn on summary prompts on individual tables so that row summaries appear on the corresponding forms and views.

select **Tables** on the left navigation pane, and then open the table where you want to configure a row summary.

claims.quote: Searched: "row summary" "AI Skill Config" Dataverse Web API configure prompt; "aiconfiguration" "row summary" API; "AI Skill Config" "Web API". Read configure-form-row-summary and AI Skill Config search excerpts; found solution transport, not an equivalent configuration call.

claims.claim: A separate switch specific to GCC and GCC High is not yet documented on either surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "GCC" "switch"; "row summaries" "GCC High" setting default. Opened record-summaries, configure-form-row-summary, copilot-hub and powerapps-us-government; no separate government-cloud switch found.

claims.claim: The expansion uses the row-summary environment control rather than a documented cloud-specific control.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose

claims.claim: That toggle does not hide Microsoft-provided summaries or summaries configured through another application or experience.

claims.claim: The Copilot hub page does not specify whether the preview user-scoping control is available in GCC or GCC High.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "GCC High" setting default; "row summaries" "GCC" "switch". Opened copilot-hub in full and powerapps-us-government; the hub's preview user-scoping section gives no GCC or GCC High availability statement.

claims.claim: The older AI insight cards location currently exposes the same row-summary control.
claims.quote: The same control is currently also available as **AI insight cards** in the environment feature settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the AI insight cards settings location will be removed in a future release.
claims.quote: The **AI insight cards** location will be removed in a future release.

claims.claim: A row-summary-specific usage report is not yet documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summary" usage report analytics column security; "row summaries" "usage" "report". Opened copilot-hub and row-summary user, maker and FAQ pages; found analytics for other AI features, not a row-summary-specific report.

claims.claim: Executing summary prompts sends record data to a generative AI service.
claims.quote: Prompt builder prompts run on Azure OpenAI Service hosted by Microsoft. Customer data isn't used to train or improve any of the Azure OpenAI Service foundation models.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining required user licences with AI Builder prompt consumption.
claims.quote: AI Builder is licensed on a capacity basis. Building custom and testing models (including prompts) doesn't require AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits. Running them in agents, agent flows, apps, or flows consume these credits.

claims.claim: Variable cost is appropriate because AI Builder prompt execution consumes AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: AI Builder features in apps and flows first try to consume AI Builder credits, then if absent or exhausted, they try to consume Copilot Credits.

claims.where: writer evidence: AI Builder building and testing
claims.claim: Building and testing AI Builder models, including prompts, does not require AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Building custom and testing models (including prompts) doesn't require AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits.
